findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when the cached group can no longer be resolved, which relocates rather than fixes the NPE: any caller that unboxes the Long (e.g. long c = group.getSubGroupsCount() or if (group.getSubGroupsCount() > 0)) will throw NPE at the call site, and no caller handling was added; should return 0L or throw the same well-defined 'entity no longer exists' exception the rest of the class produces instead of an undocumented null

[Medium/bug] The fix in GroupAdapter is point-wise rather than uniform: sibling methods that resolve the live model via getGroupModel()/modelSupplier (e.g. the getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, first, max) overloads) will still fail with an exception/NPE under the exact same concurrent-delete race; the vanished-entity case should be handled at the common resolution point (getGroupModel() or the cache lookup), otherwise concurrent group deletion still produces 500s on neighboring code paths

[Medium/test_gap] GroupTest reader thread is never joined: deletedAll.set(true) (line 155) is immediately followed by the assertion (line 157), so a request already in flight can append an exception after assertThat(caughtExceptions, empty()) executes; the test can pass while the race still reproduces, and the orphaned thread can keep issuing calls against the realm/client while teardown closes them; join the thread before asserting

[Medium/test_gap] GroupTest deletion loop (lines 152-155) is not wrapped in try/finally: if any remove() call throws, deletedAll.set(true) is never reached and the non-daemon reader thread spins forever, hanging the test (and potentially the surefire fork) instead of failing cleanly; set the flag in a finally block and/or make the thread daemon with a bounded loop

[Low/test_gap] GroupTest has no handshake (latch, or waiting for the first successful read) guaranteeing the reader thread actually runs concurrently with the deletions; under unfavorable CI scheduling the thread may not start until all 100 deletes are done, making the test pass vacuously without ever exercising the race

[Low/doc_defect] The change implicitly introduces null as a possible return value for the GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() interface method, but the contract/javadoc is not updated and other implementations (JPA, map store) and in-repo callers are not audited, leaving null semantics undefined for implementors and callers

goldens.comment: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.
The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti()`, a non-daemon reader thread is started and spins in `while (!deletedAll.get())` until `deletedAll.set(true)` is executed after the deletion loop. The deletion loop (`groupUuuids.forEach(...remove())`) is not protected by try/finally; if any `remove()` throws, `deletedAll.set(true)` is skipped, leaving the reader thread running indefinitely and potentially hanging the test process.

adjudication.rationale: In the added test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, the reader thread is started with `new Thread(...).start()` and the main thread immediately proceeds to delete all groups and then sets `deletedAll` to true. There is no latch/handshake to ensure the reader thread actually begins executing (or performs at least one read) before deletions complete, so under some scheduling it may never run concurrently and the test can pass without exercising the intended race. Additionally, there is no `join()` or other wait to ensure the reader thread has stopped before asserting `caughtExceptions` is empty, which can make the assertion timing-dependent.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()`, the diff changes the behavior from always delegating to `getGroupModel().getSubGroupsCount()` to returning `null` when `modelSupplier.get()` returns `null` (`return model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount();`). This does introduce a new, explicit `null` outcome for this `GroupModel` implementation, and the diff does not show any accompanying contract/javadoc update or caller-side handling. However, the diff alone does not prove this will break anything (the return type is already `Long`, which permits null), nor does it show other implementations/callers, so it’s best treated as a concrete API/semantics concern rather than a verified defect.
